content: Root cause: The root cause of the bug was a buffer overflow in the `ehdr_buf` array within the `NetRxPkt` structure. Originally, `ehdr_buf` was only sized to hold the Ethernet header, but when the function `eth_strip_vlan()` was called, it attempted to write both the Ethernet header and the VLAN header into this buffer. This led to memory corruption since the buffer was not sufficiently sized to accommodate both headers. The patch increased the size of `ehdr_buf` to prevent this overflow and introduced a mechanism to track the actual length of the data stored in the buffer, preventing further corruptions.

Code statements:
```c
    uint8_t ehdr_buf[sizeof(struct eth_header)];
```
```c
        pkt->vlan_stripped = eth_strip_vlan(iov, iovcnt, iovoff, pkt->ehdr_buf,
                                            &ploff, &tci);
```
```c
        pkt->vlan_stripped = false;
```
```c
    return pkt->vlan_stripped;
```
